title: EU opens accession negotiations with Ukraine and Moldova at intergovernmental conferences in Luxembourg
body:
On 25 June 2024, the European Union launched separate intergovernmental conferences with Ukraine and Moldova in Luxembourg, formally opening accession negotiations with both countries. Ukraine's delegation was led by Deputy Prime Minister for European and Euro-Atlantic integration Olga Stefanishyna, and Moldova's by Prime Minister Dorin Recean. Both countries had received candidate status in June 2022.

Starting negotiations requires the unanimous agreement of member states, endorsed by the European Council. The European Commission recommended opening the talks in November 2023, and the European Council agreed a month later. Candidates must open and then close six clusters of negotiating chapters. EU ambassadors approved the start the previous week, and officials reportedly wanted the talks to begin in June, before Hungary took over the rotating Council presidency from Belgium in July.

Stefanishyna said: "We have surpassed the barrier of promise to delivery." Commission President Ursula von der Leyen called it "very good news" and said the path ahead would be "challenging but full of opportunities". The opening placed the two countries on an equal footing with Albania and North Macedonia, whose first conferences took place in July 2022. At the time of the opening, screening was complete but no negotiating clusters had yet been opened.
